# Overview

A self-contained analysis, built from scratch, in two parts.

**Part A — Identify foraging strategies from behaviour.** Movement and diving
variables only (19 variables). PCA → number of dimensions chosen by parallel
analysis → HCPC (Ward + k-means consolidation). The number of strategies is
chosen with explicit, data-driven rules: the gap statistic, a minimum cluster
size, and bootstrap stability. Every choice is followed by a sensitivity check.

**Part B — Isotopic niches of those strategies.** Stable isotopes are **not**
used in Part A, so they are an independent test of whether behaviourally
defined strategies also differ in diet / foraging habitat: permutation tests,
effect sizes, equivalence tests and Bayesian niche size and overlap
(nicheROVER, SEA).

This is the Post-Moult version of `NESE_PB_ForagingStrategies.Rmd`: same
variables, same rules, same tests, so the two trips are directly comparable.
Differences from the Post-Breeding script: trips with impossible values are
flagged and excluded, the number of strategies is left to the decision rule,
a null-model test checks whether there is cluster structure at all, the
"one more strategy?" check is generic (K vs K + 1), and strategies are compared
with each seal's Post-Breeding strategy.

All random steps are seeded. For a first test run, lower `N_BOOT`, `N_PERM`,
`N_PA` and `N_POST` in the settings chunk.

```{r libraries}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(FactoMineR)
library(factoextra)
library(cluster)     # clusGap, silhouette
# mclust is called as mclust::adjustedRandIndex (attaching it masks dplyr::count)
library(nicheROVER)
# MASS is called as MASS:: to avoid masking dplyr::select
```

# Settings

```{r settings}
SEED <- 20261102
set.seed(SEED)

# Part A
N_DIM_OVERRIDE  <- NULL   # NULL = use parallel analysis; or set a number
K_OVERRIDE      <- NULL   # NULL = use the decision rule below; or set a number
EXCLUDE_INVALID <- TRUE   # drop trips with impossible values (percent > 100, proportion > 1)
N_NULL          <- 500    # simulations for the "is there cluster structure?" test
K_RANGE         <- 2:8    # candidate numbers of strategies
MIN_CLUSTER_N   <- 5      # smallest acceptable strategy (individuals)
MIN_JACCARD     <- 0.75   # every strategy must be at least "stable" (Hennig 2007)
N_PA            <- 1000   # parallel-analysis permutations
N_GAP           <- 200    # gap-statistic reference data sets
N_BOOT          <- 500    # bootstrap replicates for stability
SKEW_THRESHOLD  <- 1      # |skewness| above which variables are log-transformed in the sensitivity run

# Part B
N_PERM          <- 4999   # permutations for Freedman-Lane tests
N_POST          <- 1e4    # nicheROVER posterior draws
LOW_CONFIDENCE  <- 0.80   # seals with bootstrap co-assignment below this are "low confidence"

# SIBER (needs JAGS installed: https://mcmc-jags.sourceforge.io, then install.packages(c("rjags", "SIBER")))
SIBER_PARMS  <- list(n.iter = 2e4, n.burnin = 1e3, n.thin = 10, n.chains = 2)
SIBER_PRIORS <- list(R = 1 * diag(2), k = 2, tau.mu = 1.0E-3)   # SIBER defaults
SIBER_DRAWS  <- 500      # posterior draws used for Bayesian ellipse overlap
SIBER_P      <- 0.95     # ellipse used for overlap (0.95 = 95% ellipse; NULL = standard ellipse)
HAS_SIBER <- requireNamespace("SIBER", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("rjags", quietly = TRUE)
if (!HAS_SIBER) message("SIBER/rjags (JAGS) not available: the SIBER section will be skipped.")
# Equivalence margins (permil): differences smaller than these are considered
# ecologically negligible. Biological judgement - justify in the paper.
EQUIV <- c(d13C = 0.3, d15N = 0.5)

OUT <- "../results/PM_strategies"
FIG <- "../figures/PM_strategies"
# Post-Breeding assignments (from NESE_PB_ForagingStrategies.Rmd), for the PB-PM comparison
PB_ASSIGNMENTS <- "../results/PB_strategies/A_strategy_assignments.csv"
dir.create(OUT, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(FIG, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

PAL <- c("#1b9e77", "#d95f02", "#7570b3", "#e7298a", "#66a61e", "#e6ab02", "#a6761d", "#666666")
```

## Data checks

```{r checks}
# 0. Impossible values: percentages outside 0-100, proportions outside 0-1.
#    Check these trips in the raw data; by default they are excluded.
pct_vars  <- grep("^Pct", BEHAV, value = TRUE)
prop_vars <- names(REGIONS)
bad <- dat %>% dplyr::select(TOPPID, all_of(c(pct_vars, prop_vars))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-TOPPID, names_to = "variable") %>%
  filter((variable %in% pct_vars  & (value < 0 | value > 100)) |
         (variable %in% prop_vars & (value < 0 | value > 1)))
bad
if (EXCLUDE_INVALID && nrow(bad) > 0) {
  dat <- dat[!dat$TOPPID %in% bad$TOPPID, ]
  n <- nrow(dat)
  cat("Excluded", n_distinct(bad$TOPPID), "trip(s) with impossible values; n =", n, "\n")
}

# 1. Mesoecoregion proportions are compositional (they sum to 1), so one of the
#    four is redundant. PCA handles the exact linear dependence (one zero eigenvalue).
summary(rowSums(dat[names(REGIONS)]))

# 2. Dive-type percentages: check their definition if they do not sum to ~100
summary(rowSums(dat[c("Pct_TransitDives", "Pct_ForagingDives",
                      "Pct_DriftDives", "Pct_BenthicDives")]))

# 3. Skewness (PCA and Ward are least-squares methods, sensitive to long tails)
skew <- function(x) { z <- (x - mean(x)) / sd(x); mean(z^3) }
sort(round(sapply(dat[BEHAV], skew), 2))

# 4. Strongly redundant pairs (|Spearman rho| > 0.85) give extra weight to one axis
rho <- cor(dat[BEHAV], method = "spearman"); rho[upper.tri(rho, diag = TRUE)] <- NA
as.data.frame(as.table(rho)) %>% filter(abs(Freq) > 0.85) %>% arrange(desc(abs(Freq)))
```

# Part A — Foraging strategies from behaviour

## Helper functions

```{r helpers-A}
pc_scores <- function(X, nd) prcomp(X, center = TRUE, scale. = TRUE)$x[, 1:nd, drop = FALSE]

# Ward + k-means consolidation from the Ward centroids (= FactoMineR::HCPC),
# fast enough for bootstrap loops
hcpc_lite <- function(S, k) {
  cl  <- cutree(hclust(dist(S), method = "ward.D2"), k)
  cen <- apply(S, 2, function(x) tapply(x, cl, mean))
  tryCatch(kmeans(S, centers = cen, iter.max = 100)$cluster,
           error = function(e) cl)   # if consolidation empties a cluster, keep Ward
}

# HCPC's own rule for suggesting k: minimise W(k)/W(k-1)
hcpc_ratio <- function(S, ks) {
  h <- hclust(dist(S), method = "ward.D2")
  g <- sort(h$height^2 / (2 * nrow(S)), decreasing = TRUE)
  W <- sapply(1:(max(ks) + 1), function(k) sum(g[k:length(g)]))
  setNames(W[ks] / W[ks - 1], ks)
}

# Whole-pipeline bootstrap: resample seals, redo PCA + clustering.
# Returns mean Jaccard per cluster and, per seal, the proportion of resamples in
# which it stays with its full-data cluster mates (co-assignment).
boot_stability <- function(X, nd, k, B = N_BOOT) {
  ref <- hcpc_lite(pc_scores(X, nd), k); m <- nrow(X)
  J <- matrix(NA, B, k)
  co <- seen <- numeric(m)
  for (b in 1:B) {
    ix <- unique(sample(m, replace = TRUE))
    cb <- hcpc_lite(pc_scores(X[ix, , drop = FALSE], nd), k)
    for (cc in 1:k) {
      A <- ix[ref[ix] == cc]
      if (length(A)) J[b, cc] <- max(sapply(unique(cb), function(j) {
        Bj <- ix[cb == j]; length(intersect(A, Bj)) / length(union(A, Bj)) }))
    }
    lab <- setNames(cb, ix)
    for (i in ix) {
      mates <- setdiff(ix[ref[ix] == ref[i]], i)
      if (length(mates)) {
        co[i] <- co[i] + mean(lab[as.character(mates)] == lab[as.character(i)])
        seen[i] <- seen[i] + 1
      }
    }
  }
  list(ref = ref, jaccard = colMeans(J, na.rm = TRUE), coassign = co / pmax(seen, 1))
}
```

## PCA and number of dimensions

The number of dimensions is chosen by **Horn's parallel analysis**: keep a
dimension only if its eigenvalue exceeds the 95th percentile of eigenvalues
from data with the same variables but no correlation among them (each column
permuted independently). Kaiser, cumulative variance and broken stick are shown
for comparison.

```{r pca}
X <- dat[BEHAV]
res.pca.full <- PCA(X, ncp = 10, graph = FALSE)
# Eigenvalues of the correlation matrix (identical to FactoMineR's standardised PCA)
eig <- pmax(eigen(cor(X), symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values, 0)
p <- length(eig)

pa <- apply(replicate(N_PA, eigen(cor(apply(X, 2, sample)), symmetric = TRUE,
                                  only.values = TRUE)$values), 1, quantile, 0.95)
bs <- sapply(1:p, function(k) sum(1 / (k:p)))

pc_tab <- data.frame(dim = 1:p, eigenvalue = eig, pct_var = 100 * eig / sum(eig),
                     cum_pct = 100 * cumsum(eig) / sum(eig), parallel_95 = pa, broken_stick = bs)
round(head(pc_tab, 10), 3)

rules <- c(`Parallel analysis (95%)` = which(eig <= pa)[1] - 1,
           `Broken stick`            = which(eig <= bs)[1] - 1,
           `Kaiser (eigenvalue > 1)` = sum(eig > 1),
           `Cumulative >= 75%`       = which(pc_tab$cum_pct >= 75)[1])
rules
N_DIM <- if (is.null(N_DIM_OVERRIDE)) max(2, rules[["Parallel analysis (95%)"]]) else N_DIM_OVERRIDE
cat("Dimensions retained: N_DIM =", N_DIM, "(", round(pc_tab$cum_pct[N_DIM], 1), "% of variance )\n")
write.csv(pc_tab, file.path(OUT, "A_pca_dimensions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r pca-plot}
g <- pc_tab %>% filter(dim <= 10) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(eigenvalue, parallel_95, broken_stick)) %>%
  mutate(name = recode(name, eigenvalue = "Observed", parallel_95 = "Parallel analysis (95%)",
                       broken_stick = "Broken stick")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(dim, value, colour = name, linetype = name)) + geom_line() + geom_point() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = N_DIM + 0.5, colour = "grey50", linetype = 3) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("black", "#d95f02", "#1b9e77")) +
  labs(x = "Dimension", y = "Eigenvalue", colour = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  theme_bw() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
g
ggsave(file.path(FIG, "A_pca_dimensions.pdf"), g, width = 7, height = 4.5)
```

### What the dimensions represent

Correlations between variables and dimensions (unrotated; these are the axes
used for clustering). Only the first two axes are usually stable enough to be
interpreted one by one — describe strategies with the original variables
(below) rather than by individual dimensions.

```{r loadings}
round(res.pca.full$var$cor[, 1:N_DIM], 2)
fviz_pca_var(res.pca.full, repel = TRUE, col.var = "contrib",
             gradient.cols = c("grey70", "#d95f02"))
```

## Number of strategies

Candidate solutions k = `r min(K_RANGE)`–`r max(K_RANGE)` are compared with:

* **Gap statistic** (Tibshirani et al. 2001, 1-SE rule): compares within-cluster
  dispersion with that of structureless reference data.
* **HCPC's own rule** (minimum within-inertia ratio), shown for information.
* **Mean silhouette** and **minimum cluster size**.
* **Bootstrap stability**: mean Jaccard similarity of each cluster across
  `r N_BOOT` resamples of the whole pipeline.

**Decision rule.** Take the k suggested by the gap statistic, provided every
strategy has ≥ `MIN_CLUSTER_N` seals and a mean Jaccard ≥ `MIN_JACCARD`.
Otherwise take the largest k below it that meets both conditions.

```{r choose-k}
S <- res.pca.full$ind$coord[, 1:N_DIM]

gs <- clusGap(S, FUNcluster = function(x, k) list(cluster = hcpc_lite(x, k)),
              K.max = max(K_RANGE), B = N_GAP, spaceH0 = "scaledPCA", verbose = FALSE)
k_gap <- maxSE(gs$Tab[, "gap"], gs$Tab[, "SE.sim"], method = "Tibs2001SEmax")
hr <- hcpc_ratio(S, K_RANGE)

stab <- lapply(K_RANGE, function(k) { set.seed(SEED); boot_stability(X, N_DIM, k) })
names(stab) <- K_RANGE

k_tab <- data.frame(
  k = K_RANGE,
  gap = gs$Tab[K_RANGE, "gap"], gap_se = gs$Tab[K_RANGE, "SE.sim"],
  hcpc_ratio = hr,
  silhouette = sapply(K_RANGE, function(k) mean(silhouette(hcpc_lite(S, k), dist(S))[, 3])),
  sizes = sapply(stab, function(s) paste(sort(table(s$ref), decreasing = TRUE), collapse = "/")),
  min_size = sapply(stab, function(s) min(table(s$ref))),
  min_jaccard = sapply(stab, function(s) min(s$jaccard)),
  row.names = NULL)
k_tab$passes <- k_tab$min_size >= MIN_CLUSTER_N & k_tab$min_jaccard >= MIN_JACCARD
k_tab %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
write.csv(k_tab, file.path(OUT, "A_number_of_strategies.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

ok <- k_tab$k[k_tab$passes]
K_SUGGESTED <- if (k_gap %in% ok) k_gap else if (any(ok < k_gap)) max(ok[ok < k_gap]) else min(K_RANGE)
K <- if (is.null(K_OVERRIDE)) K_SUGGESTED else K_OVERRIDE
cat("Gap statistic suggests k =", k_gap, "; HCPC rule suggests k =", names(which.min(hr)),
    "; decision rule gives K =", K_SUGGESTED, "; using K =", K, "\n")
```

```{r choose-k-plot, fig.height = 6}
kp <- k_tab %>% dplyr::select(k, gap, silhouette, min_jaccard) %>%
  pivot_longer(-k) %>%
  mutate(name = recode(name, gap = "Gap statistic", silhouette = "Mean silhouette",
                       min_jaccard = "Least stable cluster (Jaccard)"))
g <- ggplot(kp, aes(k, value)) + geom_line() + geom_point() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = K, colour = "#d95f02", linetype = 2) +
  geom_hline(data = data.frame(name = "Least stable cluster (Jaccard)", y = MIN_JACCARD),
             aes(yintercept = y), linetype = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~ name, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = K_RANGE) + theme_bw() + labs(x = "Number of strategies", y = NULL)
g
ggsave(file.path(FIG, "A_number_of_strategies.pdf"), g, width = 6, height = 7)
```

## Is there cluster structure at all?

Clustering always returns groups, even from a continuum. Here the observed
silhouette is compared with that obtained by applying the same clustering to
`r N_NULL` data sets simulated from a single multivariate normal distribution
with the observed variance on each retained dimension (no groups). A p-value
near or above 0.05 means the strategies are weakly separated and should be
described as modes of a continuum rather than discrete groups.

```{r null-structure}
sds <- apply(S, 2, sd)
set.seed(SEED)
null_struct <- do.call(rbind, lapply(intersect(2:4, K_RANGE), function(k) {
  obs <- mean(silhouette(hcpc_lite(S, k), dist(S))[, 3])
  sim <- replicate(N_NULL, {
    Y <- sapply(sds, function(s) rnorm(nrow(S), 0, s))
    mean(silhouette(hcpc_lite(Y, k), dist(Y))[, 3])
  })
  data.frame(k = k, silhouette = obs, null_median = median(sim),
             null_95 = quantile(sim, 0.95), p = (1 + sum(sim >= obs)) / (N_NULL + 1))
}))
rownames(null_struct) <- NULL
null_struct %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
write.csv(null_struct, file.path(OUT, "A_null_structure_test.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Would one more strategy be justified? (K vs K + 1)

When two solutions are close, the choice should rest on (i) whether the finer
solution is a refinement of the coarser one, (ii) whether the extra group is
reproducible, and (iii) whether it differs in variables that were **not** used
to build the clusters (external validation; Hennig 2015, *Pattern Recognition
Letters* 64:53–62).

### 1. What the gap statistic says

The 1-SE rule picks the *smallest* k whose gap is within one standard error of
the next; it is deliberately conservative. Other standard rules are shown for
comparison.

```{r kplus1-gap}
K_HI <- K + 1
sapply(c("Tibs2001SEmax", "firstSEmax", "firstmax", "globalSEmax", "globalmax"),
       function(m) maxSE(gs$Tab[, "gap"], gs$Tab[, "SE.sim"], method = m))
k_tab %>% filter(k %in% (K - 1):(K + 2)) %>%
  dplyr::select(k, gap, gap_se, silhouette, sizes, min_size, min_jaccard, passes) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

### 2. Is K + 1 a refinement of K, and is the extra group stable?

```{r kplus1-nesting}
stopifnot(as.character(K_HI) %in% names(stab))
l_lo <- stab[[as.character(K)]]$ref; l_hi <- stab[[as.character(K_HI)]]$ref
table(`K` = l_lo, `K + 1` = l_hi)
new_grp   <- as.integer(names(which.min(table(l_hi))))                  # smallest group at K + 1
parent    <- as.integer(names(which.max(table(l_lo[l_hi == new_grp])))) # K cluster it comes from
in_parent <- l_lo == parent
split_grp <- l_hi == new_grp & in_parent
cat("K + 1 =", K_HI, "separates", sum(split_grp), "seals from a cluster of", sum(in_parent),
    "; Jaccard stability of that group:", round(stab[[as.character(K_HI)]]$jaccard[new_grp], 2), "\n")

data.frame(scale(dat[BEHAV]))[in_parent, ] %>%
  mutate(group = ifelse(split_grp[in_parent], "split-off group", "rest of parent")) %>%
  group_by(group) %>% summarise(across(everything(), mean)) %>%
  pivot_longer(-group, names_to = "variable") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = value) %>%
  mutate(difference_z = `split-off group` - `rest of parent`) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(difference_z))) %>% head(8) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 2)))
```

### 3. External validation of the extra group

Permutation test (difference in means, two-sided) between the split-off group
and the rest of the cluster it comes from, on variables not used for clustering.

```{r kplus1-external}
perm_diff <- function(x, g, B = N_PERM) {
  obs  <- mean(x[g]) - mean(x[!g])
  null <- replicate(B, { s <- sample(g); mean(x[s]) - mean(x[!s]) })
  c(n_split = sum(g), n_rest = sum(!g),
    mean_split = mean(x[g]), mean_rest = mean(x[!g]),
    difference = obs, p_perm = (1 + sum(abs(null) >= abs(obs))) / (B + 1))
}
ext_vars <- intersect(c("TripDuration_days", "MassGainRate_kgPerDay_Dcrocker", ISO), names(dat))
set.seed(SEED)
split_tests <- t(sapply(ext_vars, function(v) {
  ok <- in_parent & !is.na(dat[[v]])
  perm_diff(dat[[v]][ok], split_grp[ok])
}))
round(split_tests, 4)
write.csv(split_tests, file.path(OUT, "A_K_vs_Kplus1_external_validation.csv"))
```

**Interpretation.** Keep K unless the extra group at K + 1 is nested, stable
(Jaccard ≥ `MIN_JACCARD`) **and** differs in independent variables. If it fails
these checks, the finer solution is splitting a continuum.

## Final HCPC

```{r hcpc}
res.pca  <- PCA(X, ncp = N_DIM, graph = FALSE)
res.hcpc <- HCPC(res.pca, nb.clust = K, consol = TRUE, graph = FALSE)
cl <- as.integer(res.hcpc$data.clust$clust)
ref_K <- stab[[as.character(K)]]$ref
cat("Agreement with the bootstrap reference partition (ARI):",
    round(mclust::adjustedRandIndex(cl, ref_K), 3), "\n")
# Jaccard values re-indexed to the HCPC cluster numbers
jac_cl <- stab[[as.character(K)]]$jaccard[
  sapply(1:K, function(j) as.integer(names(which.max(table(ref_K[cl == j])))))]

# Name each strategy by the mesoecoregion it uses most (relative to the population),
# and order strategies by size. Edit the names after looking at the profiles if needed.
zreg <- apply(scale(dat[names(REGIONS)]), 2, function(z) tapply(z, cl, mean))
nm <- make.unique(unname(REGIONS[apply(zreg, 1, which.max)]), sep = " ")
size_order <- order(table(cl), decreasing = TRUE)
dat$strategy <- factor(nm[cl], levels = nm[size_order])
COLS <- setNames(PAL[seq_len(K)], levels(dat$strategy))
table(dat$strategy)

# Per-seal assignment confidence
dat$silhouette <- silhouette(cl, dist(S))[, 3]
dat$coassign   <- stab[[as.character(K)]]$coassign
data.frame(strategy = levels(dat$strategy),
           n = as.vector(table(dat$strategy)),
           jaccard = jac_cl[size_order],
           median_coassign = tapply(dat$coassign, dat$strategy, median),
           n_low_confidence = tapply(dat$coassign < LOW_CONFIDENCE, dat$strategy, sum)) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 2)))
dat %>% filter(coassign < LOW_CONFIDENCE | silhouette < 0) %>%
  dplyr::select(TOPPID, ProcedureYear, strategy, silhouette, coassign)
```

```{r hcpc-plots, fig.height = 6}
fviz_dend(res.hcpc, cex = 0.5, palette = unname(PAL[seq_len(K)]), rect = TRUE,
          rect_fill = TRUE, show_labels = FALSE, main = "Post-Moult females: HCPC")
```

## Sensitivity of the strategies

Each alternative is compared with the final partition with the adjusted Rand
index (ARI = 1: identical; > 0.8: very similar).

```{r sensitivity}
ari <- function(a, b) round(mclust::adjustedRandIndex(a, b), 3)
sens <- list()

for (nd in setdiff(c(N_DIM - 1, N_DIM + 1, length(BEHAV)), 1))
  sens[[paste("Dimensions =", nd)]] <- ari(cl, hcpc_lite(pc_scores(X, nd), K))

mfa <- MFA(X, group = c(length(SPACE), length(DIVE)), type = c("s", "s"),
           name.group = c("Space", "Diving"), ncp = N_DIM, graph = FALSE)
sens[["MFA (blocks weighted equally)"]] <- ari(cl, hcpc_lite(mfa$ind$coord[, 1:N_DIM], K))

sk <- names(which(abs(sapply(X, skew)) > SKEW_THRESHOLD & sapply(X, min) >= 0))
Xlog <- X; Xlog[sk] <- lapply(X[sk], function(x) log(x + max(min(x[x > 0]) / 2, 1e-6)))
sens[["Log-transform skewed variables"]] <- ari(cl, hcpc_lite(pc_scores(Xlog, N_DIM), K))

Xred <- X[setdiff(BEHAV, c("SdDistContShelf_km", "MesoEcoProportionNorthCPac"))]
sens[["Drop redundant SdDist + NorthCPac"]] <- ari(cl, hcpc_lite(pc_scores(Xred, N_DIM), K))

sens[["Ward without consolidation"]] <- ari(cl, cutree(hclust(dist(S), "ward.D2"), K))
set.seed(SEED)
sens[["k-means (100 starts)"]] <- ari(cl, kmeans(S, K, nstart = 100)$cluster)

md2 <- mahalanobis(S, colMeans(S), cov(S))
out <- md2 > qchisq(0.999, N_DIM)
cat("Multivariate outliers (p < 0.001):", paste(dat$TOPPID[out], collapse = ", "), "\n")
if (any(out)) sens[["Without multivariate outliers"]] <-
  ari(cl[!out], hcpc_lite(pc_scores(X[!out, ], N_DIM), K))

one <- !duplicated(ifelse(is.na(dat$MainID), dat$TOPPID, dat$MainID))
sens[["One trip per seal"]] <- ari(cl[one], hcpc_lite(pc_scores(X[one, ], N_DIM), K))

sens_tab <- data.frame(scenario = names(sens), ARI = unlist(sens), row.names = NULL)
sens_tab
write.csv(sens_tab, file.path(OUT, "A_sensitivity.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(dat %>% dplyr::select(TOPPID, MainID, ProcedureYear, strategy, silhouette, coassign),
          file.path(OUT, "A_strategy_assignments.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## Comparison with the Post-Breeding strategies

For seals tracked on both trips, is the Post-Moult strategy related to the
Post-Breeding one? Run `NESE_PB_ForagingStrategies.Rmd` first. Only a subset of
seals have both trips, so treat this as exploratory. The PB and PM trips
compared here need not be from the same year.

```{r pb-pm}
if (file.exists(PB_ASSIGNMENTS)) {
  yr <- function(x) as.integer(as.character(x))
  pb <- read.csv(PB_ASSIGNMENTS) %>%
    mutate(MainID = as.character(MainID), PB_year = yr(ProcedureYear),
           PB_strategy = as.character(strategy)) %>%
    filter(!is.na(MainID)) %>% arrange(PB_year) %>%
    dplyr::select(MainID, TOPPID_PB = TOPPID, PB_year, PB_strategy)
  pm <- dat %>% filter(!is.na(MainID)) %>%
    transmute(MainID, TOPPID_PM = TOPPID, PM_year = yr(ProcedureYear),
              PM_strategy = as.character(strategy)) %>%
    arrange(PM_year)

  # All PB-PM trip pairs, for reference (seals with repeated trips appear more than once)
  print(inner_join(pm, pb, by = "MainID"))

  # Analysis unit = seal: earliest PM trip paired with earliest PB trip
  both <- inner_join(distinct(pm, MainID, .keep_all = TRUE),
                     distinct(pb, MainID, .keep_all = TRUE), by = "MainID")
  cat(nrow(both), "seals with both a PB and a PM trip (one pair per seal)\n")
  tab <- table(PB = both$PB_strategy, PM = both$PM_strategy)
  print(tab)
  if (nrow(both) >= 5 && all(dim(tab) > 1))
    print(fisher.test(tab, simulate.p.value = TRUE, B = 1e4))

  # Same offshore region on both trips? (seals whose PB strategy also exists after the moult)
  sh <- both %>% filter(PB_strategy %in% levels(dat$strategy))
  if (nrow(sh) >= 3) {
    obs <- sum(sh$PB_strategy == sh$PM_strategy)
    set.seed(SEED)
    null <- replicate(N_PERM, sum(sh$PB_strategy == sample(sh$PM_strategy)))
    cat(obs, "of", nrow(sh), "seals used the same region on both trips; expected by chance",
        round(mean(null), 1), "; P =", signif((1 + sum(null >= obs)) / (N_PERM + 1), 3), "\n")
  }
  write.csv(both, file.path(OUT, "A_PB_PM_per_seal.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  message("PB assignments not found at ", PB_ASSIGNMENTS, ": run the PB script first.")
}
```

# Part B — Isotopic niches of the strategies

Isotopes were not used to define the strategies, so differences here are an
independent result. State which tissue was sampled and the period it integrates
relative to the tracked trip. Isotopic baselines vary among years, so year is
included as a covariate in the tests and checked in the sensitivity analysis.

## Helper functions

```{r helpers-B}
# Freedman-Lane permutation F test for `term`, adjusting for `covars`
fl_test <- function(d, response, term = "strategy", covars = character(0), B = N_PERM) {
  v  <- c(response, term, covars)
  d  <- d[complete.cases(d[v]), v, drop = FALSE]
  X0 <- model.matrix(reformulate(if (length(covars)) covars else "1"), d)
  X1 <- model.matrix(reformulate(c(covars, term)), d)
  y  <- d[[response]]
  Fstat <- function(y) {
    m0 <- lm.fit(X0, y); m1 <- lm.fit(X1, y)
    r0 <- sum(m0$residuals^2); r1 <- sum(m1$residuals^2)
    ((r0 - r1) / (m1$rank - m0$rank)) / (r1 / (nrow(X1) - m1$rank))
  }
  F_obs <- Fstat(y)
  m0 <- lm.fit(X0, y); fit0 <- y - m0$residuals
  F_p <- replicate(B, Fstat(fit0 + sample(m0$residuals)))
  data.frame(response = response,
             covariates = if (length(covars)) paste(covars, collapse = " + ") else "none",
             n = nrow(d), F = F_obs, p_perm = (1 + sum(F_p >= F_obs)) / (B + 1))
}

# All pairwise differences between strategies from an lm, with CIs
pair_contrasts <- function(fit, term = "strategy", level = 0.95) {
  b <- coef(fit); V <- vcov(fit)
  lev <- levels(model.frame(fit)[[term]]); cn <- paste0(term, lev)
  tq <- qt(1 - (1 - level) / 2, fit$df.residual)
  do.call(rbind, combn(seq_along(lev), 2, simplify = FALSE, FUN = function(ij) {
    L <- setNames(numeric(length(b)), names(b))
    if (cn[ij[2]] %in% names(b)) L[cn[ij[2]]] <- 1
    if (cn[ij[1]] %in% names(b)) L[cn[ij[1]]] <- L[cn[ij[1]]] - 1
    est <- sum(L * b); se <- sqrt(drop(t(L) %*% V %*% L))
    data.frame(contrast = paste(lev[ij[2]], "-", lev[ij[1]]),
               estimate = est, lwr = est - tq * se, upr = est + tq * se)
  }))
}

# Bayesian niche summaries (nicheROVER, default non-informative prior)
iso_niche <- function(d, nsamples = N_POST, seed = SEED) {
  set.seed(seed)
  par <- tapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), droplevels(d$strategy),
                function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = nsamples, X = as.matrix(d[ii, ISO])))
  nr95 <- sapply(par, function(sp) apply(sp$Sigma, 3, niche.size, alpha = 0.95))
  seab <- sapply(par, function(sp) apply(sp$Sigma, 3, function(Sg) pi * sqrt(det(Sg))))
  set.seed(seed)
  ov <- overlap(par, nreps = nsamples, nprob = nsamples, alpha = c(0.95, 0.99))
  list(par = par, nr95 = nr95, seab = seab, overlap = ov)
}
```

## Do strategies differ in isotopic values?

```{r iso-tests}
set.seed(SEED)
iso_tests <- bind_rows(lapply(ISO, function(v) bind_rows(
  fl_test(dat, v), fl_test(dat, v, covars = "ProcedureYear"))))
iso_tests$p_BH <- p.adjust(iso_tests$p_perm, "BH")
iso_tests %>% mutate(across(c(F, p_perm, p_BH), ~ signif(.x, 3)))

fits <- lapply(setNames(ISO, ISO), function(v)
  lm(reformulate(c("strategy", "ProcedureYear"), v), data = dat))
contr <- bind_rows(lapply(fits, pair_contrasts), .id = "isotope")
contr %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
write.csv(bind_rows(iso_tests), file.path(OUT, "B_isotope_tests.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(contr, file.path(OUT, "B_isotope_contrasts.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

### Isotopic differences with K - 1, K and K + 1 strategies

```{r iso-k-compare}
set.seed(SEED)
bind_rows(lapply(intersect(c(K - 1, K, K + 1), K_RANGE), function(k) {
  d <- dat; d$strategy <- factor(stab[[as.character(k)]]$ref)
  bind_rows(lapply(ISO, function(v) fl_test(d, v, covars = "ProcedureYear"))) %>% mutate(k = k)
})) %>% dplyr::select(k, response, n, F, p_perm) %>% mutate(across(c(F, p_perm), ~ signif(.x, 3)))
```

### Equivalence: are some strategies isotopically indistinguishable?

A non-significant test is not evidence of no difference. Two one-sided tests
(TOST): two strategies are considered equivalent if the 90 % CI of their
difference lies inside ±margin (`EQUIV`).

```{r iso-equivalence}
tost <- bind_rows(lapply(ISO, function(v) {
  ci <- pair_contrasts(fits[[v]], level = 0.90)
  data.frame(isotope = v, ci, margin = EQUIV[[v]],
             equivalent = ci$lwr > -EQUIV[[v]] & ci$upr < EQUIV[[v]],
             different  = ci$lwr > 0 | ci$upr < 0)
}))
tost %>% mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))
```

## Isotopic niche size and overlap (nicheROVER)

nicheROVER is used with its **default, non-informative prior** and a fixed
seed. Niche size is reported as the 95 % niche region (nicheROVER) and as the
Bayesian standard ellipse area (SEA_B = π√|Σ|, comparable with SIBER); SEAc is
the small-sample-corrected standard ellipse area from the data.

```{r iso-niche}
nb <- iso_niche(dat)

sea_c <- tapply(seq_len(n), dat$strategy, function(ii) {
  m <- length(ii); pi * sqrt(det(cov(dat[ii, ISO]))) * (m - 1) / (m - 2) })
size_tab <- data.frame(strategy = levels(dat$strategy), n = as.vector(table(dat$strategy)),
  SEAc = as.vector(sea_c),
  SEAb_median = apply(nb$seab, 2, median),
  SEAb_lwr = apply(nb$seab, 2, quantile, 0.025), SEAb_upr = apply(nb$seab, 2, quantile, 0.975),
  NR95_median = apply(nb$nr95, 2, median),
  NR95_lwr = apply(nb$nr95, 2, quantile, 0.025), NR95_upr = apply(nb$nr95, 2, quantile, 0.975))
size_tab %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
write.csv(size_tab, file.path(OUT, "B_niche_size.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Posterior probability that the row strategy has a larger niche than the column strategy
lev <- levels(dat$strategy)
round(outer(lev, lev, Vectorize(function(a, b) mean(nb$seab[, a] > nb$seab[, b]))), 3) %>%
  `dimnames<-`(list(lev, lev))
```

```{r iso-size-plot}

  mutate(strategy = factor(strategy, lev)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(strategy, value, fill = strategy)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.6, colour = NA) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = function(x) data.frame(y = median(x), ymin = quantile(x, .025),
                                                 ymax = quantile(x, .975))) +
  geom_point(data = size_tab, aes(strategy, SEAc), shape = 4, size = 3, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = COLS, guide = "none") + theme_bw() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = expression("SEA"[B]~"(‰"^2*")"),
       caption = "Median and 95% credible interval; x = SEAc")

ggsave(file.path(FIG, "B_niche_size.pdf"), g, width = 6, height = 4.5, device = cairo_pdf)
```

**Overlap.** Entry [row, column] is the probability (%) that an individual of
the row strategy falls inside the 95 % niche region of the column strategy.
Overlap is directional, so the two directions can differ.

```{r iso-overlap}
ov_mean <- apply(nb$overlap, c(1:2, 4), mean) * 100
ov_ci   <- apply(nb$overlap * 100, c(1:2, 4), quantile, prob = c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)
round(ov_mean[, , 1], 1)
round(ov_ci[, , , 1], 1)
ov_long <- expand.grid(from = lev, into = lev, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>% filter(from != into) %>%
  mutate(mean = mapply(function(a, b) ov_mean[a, b, 1], from, into),
         lwr  = mapply(function(a, b) ov_ci[1, a, b, 1], from, into),
         upr  = mapply(function(a, b) ov_ci[2, a, b, 1], from, into))
write.csv(ov_long, file.path(OUT, "B_niche_overlap_95.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r iso-niche-plots, fig.height = 6}
                function(ii) niw.post(nsamples = 50, X = as.matrix(dat[ii, ISO])))
dat_l <- tapply(seq_len(n), dat$strategy, function(ii) as.matrix(dat[ii, ISO]))
niche.plot(niche.par = par50, niche.data = dat_l, pfrac = 0.05,
```

## Isotopic niche size and overlap (SIBER)

SIBER (Jackson et al. 2011) gives the standard measures of isotopic niche
width: the sample-size-corrected standard ellipse area (SEAc) and its Bayesian
estimate (SEA_B, fitted in JAGS). Overlap is the **area** shared by two
ellipses (here the `r SIBER_P * 100` % ellipses), expressed as a proportion of
the combined area (symmetric) and of each ellipse (directional). Unlike
nicheROVER's probabilistic overlap, it is purely geometric, so the two are not
directly comparable. This section is skipped if JAGS is not installed.

```{r siber-fit, eval = HAS_SIBER}
# SIBER needs columns iso1, iso2, group, community; simple group codes avoid
# problems with spaces in names (lookup table below)
codes <- setNames(paste0("S", seq_along(lev)), lev)
siber_df <- data.frame(iso1 = dat$d13C, iso2 = dat$d15N,
                       group = unname(codes[as.character(dat$strategy)]), community = 1)
siber <- SIBER::createSiberObject(siber_df)
ell_id <- paste0("1.", codes)                 # ellipse identifiers: "community.group"
names(ell_id) <- lev
data.frame(strategy = lev, code = codes, ellipse = ell_id, row.names = NULL)

# Maximum-likelihood metrics (TA = convex hull area, SEA, SEAc)
ml <- SIBER::groupMetricsML(siber)
colnames(ml) <- lev[match(colnames(ml), ell_id)]
round(ml, 3)

# Bayesian standard ellipses
set.seed(SEED)
ell_post <- SIBER::siberMVN(siber, SIBER_PARMS, SIBER_PRIORS)
sea_b_siber <- SIBER::siberEllipses(ell_post)
colnames(sea_b_siber) <- lev[match(names(ell_post), ell_id)]

siber_size <- data.frame(strategy = colnames(sea_b_siber),
  n = as.vector(table(dat$strategy)[colnames(sea_b_siber)]),
  SEAc = ml["SEAc", colnames(sea_b_siber)],
  SEAb_mode = apply(sea_b_siber, 2, function(x) { dd <- density(x); dd$x[which.max(dd$y)] }),
  SEAb_median = apply(sea_b_siber, 2, median),
  SEAb_lwr = apply(sea_b_siber, 2, quantile, 0.025),
  SEAb_upr = apply(sea_b_siber, 2, quantile, 0.975), row.names = NULL)
siber_size %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
write.csv(siber_size, file.path(OUT, "B_SIBER_niche_size.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

# Posterior probability that the row strategy has a larger SEA_B than the column strategy
round(outer(colnames(sea_b_siber), colnames(sea_b_siber),
            Vectorize(function(a, b) mean(sea_b_siber[, a] > sea_b_siber[, b]))), 3) %>%
  `dimnames<-`(list(colnames(sea_b_siber), colnames(sea_b_siber)))
```

```{r siber-plots, eval = HAS_SIBER, fig.height = 5}
par(mfrow = c(1, 2), mar = c(4.5, 4.5, 1, 1))
SIBER::plotSiberObject(siber, ax.pad = 0.5, hulls = FALSE, ellipses = TRUE,
                       group.ellipses.args = list(lty = 1, lwd = 2, p.interval = SIBER_P),
                       group.hulls = FALSE, bty = "L", iso.order = c(1, 2),
                       xlab = expression(delta^{13}*C~"(‰)"),
                       ylab = expression(delta^{15}*N~"(‰)"))
legend("topleft", legend = paste(codes, names(codes)), bty = "n", cex = 0.7)
SIBER::siberDensityPlot(sea_b_siber, xticklabels = codes[colnames(sea_b_siber)],
                        xlab = "Strategy", ylab = expression("SEA"[B]~"(‰"^2*")"))
points(seq_len(ncol(sea_b_siber)), siber_size$SEAc, col = "red", pch = 4, lwd = 2)
par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r siber-overlap, eval = HAS_SIBER}
pairs_s <- combn(lev, 2, simplify = FALSE)

# Maximum-likelihood overlap of the ellipses
ml_ov <- do.call(rbind, lapply(pairs_s, function(pr) {
  o <- SIBER::maxLikOverlap(ell_id[pr[1]], ell_id[pr[2]], siber, p.interval = SIBER_P, n = 100)
  data.frame(A = pr[1], B = pr[2], area_A = o[["area.1"]], area_B = o[["area.2"]],
             overlap_area = o[["overlap"]])
}))

# Bayesian overlap: one value per posterior draw
set.seed(SEED)
bayes_ov <- lapply(pairs_s, function(pr)
  SIBER::bayesianOverlap(ell_id[pr[1]], ell_id[pr[2]], ell_post,
                         draws = SIBER_DRAWS, p.interval = SIBER_P, n = 100))
names(bayes_ov) <- sapply(pairs_s, paste, collapse = " vs ")

q3 <- function(x) sprintf("%.2f (%.2f-%.2f)", median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
                          quantile(x, 0.025, na.rm = TRUE), quantile(x, 0.975, na.rm = TRUE))
siber_ov <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(pairs_s), function(i) {
  b <- bayes_ov[[i]]; pr <- pairs_s[[i]]
  ml_i <- ml_ov[i, ]
  data.frame(
    A = pr[1], B = pr[2],
    ML_prop_of_union = ml_i$overlap_area / (ml_i$area_A + ml_i$area_B - ml_i$overlap_area),
    Bayes_prop_of_union = q3(b$overlap / (b$area1 + b$area2 - b$overlap)),
    Bayes_prop_of_A = q3(b$overlap / b$area1),     # share of A's ellipse inside B's
    Bayes_prop_of_B = q3(b$overlap / b$area2))     # share of B's ellipse inside A's
}))
siber_ov %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
write.csv(siber_ov, file.path(OUT, "B_SIBER_overlap.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r siber-overlap-plot, eval = HAS_SIBER, fig.height = 4}
g <- bind_rows(lapply(names(bayes_ov), function(nm) {
  b <- bayes_ov[[nm]]
  data.frame(pair = nm, prop = b$overlap / (b$area1 + b$area2 - b$overlap))
})) %>%
  ggplot(aes(pair, prop)) + geom_violin(fill = "grey80", colour = NA) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = function(x) data.frame(y = median(x), ymin = quantile(x, .025),
                                                 ymax = quantile(x, .975))) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) + theme_bw() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Overlap (proportion of combined ellipse area)",
       caption = paste0(SIBER_P * 100, "% ellipses; median and 95% credible interval"))
g
ggsave(file.path(FIG, "B_SIBER_overlap.pdf"), g, width = 7, height = 4)
```

**Reading the two approaches together.** Use SEAc / SEA_B (SIBER) to report
niche width, and nicheROVER's directional probabilities as the main overlap
result, with SIBER's area overlap as a check. They should agree on which pairs
overlap most, even though the values differ. With only a handful of seals in
the smallest strategy, its ellipse and every overlap involving it are
uncertain; report the credible intervals.

## Sensitivity of the isotopic results

* **One trip per seal** — removes repeated individuals.
* **High-confidence seals only** — bootstrap co-assignment ≥ `LOW_CONFIDENCE`.
* **Year-centred isotopes** — removes year-to-year baseline shifts. Note that
  this also removes any real difference between strategies that happen to be
  concentrated in particular years.

```{r iso-sensitivity}
iso_c <- dat %>% group_by(ProcedureYear) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(ISO), ~ .x - mean(.x))) %>% ungroup() %>% as.data.frame()
subsets <- list(`All trips` = dat,
                `One trip per seal` = dat[one, ],
                `High-confidence seals` = dat[dat$coassign >= LOW_CONFIDENCE, ],
                `Year-centred isotopes` = iso_c)

summ_subset <- function(d, nsamples = 5000) {
  d$strategy <- droplevels(d$strategy)
  if (min(table(d$strategy)) < 4) return(NULL)
  nbx <- iso_niche(d, nsamples)
  ov  <- apply(nbx$overlap, c(1:2, 4), mean)[, , 1] * 100
  set.seed(SEED)
  tests <- sapply(ISO, function(v) fl_test(d, v, covars = "ProcedureYear", B = 1999)$p_perm)
  list(n = table(d$strategy),
       SEAb_median = round(apply(nbx$seab, 2, median), 3),
       overlap95 = round(ov, 1),
       p_strategy_given_year = signif(tests, 3))
}
sens_iso <- lapply(subsets, summ_subset)
sens_iso
```

# Part C — Post-Moult behaviour as a continuum

Post-moult groups are only weakly separated (Section "Is there cluster
structure at all?"), so the more natural analysis is to relate isotopes to each
seal's **position along the behavioural gradient** (its scores on the retained
PCA axes) rather than to group labels. If the gradient explains isotopes better
than the two modes do, post-moult foraging is best described as a continuum.

## The behavioural gradient

```{r gradient-axes}
G <- as.data.frame(res.pca$ind$coord[, 1:N_DIM]); names(G) <- paste0("Dim", 1:N_DIM)
DIMS <- names(G)
gd <- cbind(dat[, c("TOPPID", "MainID", "ProcedureYear", "strategy", ISO, "MesoEcoProportionCAC")], G)
cac_min <- min(gd$MesoEcoProportionCAC[gd$MesoEcoProportionCAC > 0])
gd$logCAC <- log(gd$MesoEcoProportionCAC + cac_min / 2)

# What each axis represents (variable-axis correlations, |r| >= 0.5)
cor_tab <- res.pca$var$cor[, 1:N_DIM]; colnames(cor_tab) <- DIMS
lapply(setNames(DIMS, DIMS), function(d) { r <- cor_tab[, d]; round(sort(r[abs(r) >= 0.5]), 2) })
```

```{r gradient-distribution, fig.height = 4}
g <- ggplot(gd, aes(Dim1, fill = strategy)) + geom_histogram(bins = 25, colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = COLS) + theme_bw() +
  labs(x = sprintf("Dim 1 score (%.1f%% of variance)", pc_tab$pct_var[1]),
       y = "Number of trips", fill = "Mode")
g
ggsave(file.path(FIG, "C_gradient_distribution.pdf"), g, width = 7, height = 4)

# Hartigan's dip test of unimodality along the main axis (needs the 'diptest' package)
if (requireNamespace("diptest", quietly = TRUE)) diptest::dip.test(gd$Dim1) else
  message("Install the 'diptest' package for a formal test of unimodality.")
```

## Do isotopes vary along the gradient?

Each axis is tested while adjusting for the other axes and for year
(Freedman–Lane permutation tests), so each test asks whether that dimension of
behaviour explains isotopic variation on its own.

```{r gradient-isotopes}
set.seed(SEED)
grad_tests <- bind_rows(lapply(ISO, function(v) bind_rows(lapply(DIMS, function(d)
  fl_test(gd, v, term = d, covars = c(setdiff(DIMS, d), "ProcedureYear")) %>% mutate(term = d)))))
grad_tests$p_BH <- p.adjust(grad_tests$p_perm, "BH")
grad_tests %>% dplyr::select(response, term, n, F, p_perm, p_BH) %>%
  mutate(across(c(F, p_perm, p_BH), ~ signif(.x, 3)))

# Slopes (permil per unit of axis score) with 95% CIs
grad_fits <- lapply(setNames(ISO, ISO), function(v)
  lm(reformulate(c(DIMS, "ProcedureYear"), v), data = gd))
grad_slopes <- bind_rows(lapply(names(grad_fits), function(v) {
  f <- grad_fits[[v]]; ci <- confint(f)[DIMS, , drop = FALSE]
  data.frame(isotope = v, axis = DIMS, slope = unname(coef(f)[DIMS]),
             lwr = unname(ci[, 1]), upr = unname(ci[, 2]))
}))
grad_slopes %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
write.csv(grad_tests, file.path(OUT, "C_isotopes_vs_gradient_tests.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(grad_slopes, file.path(OUT, "C_isotopes_vs_gradient_slopes.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

California Current use is the clearest single behavioural correlate of
isotopic enrichment in both trips, so it is also tested directly (log scale,
adjusting for year).

```{r gradient-cac}
set.seed(SEED)
cac_tests <- bind_rows(lapply(ISO, function(v) fl_test(gd, v, term = "logCAC", covars = "ProcedureYear")))
cac_tests %>% mutate(across(c(F, p_perm), ~ signif(.x, 3)))
sapply(setNames(ISO, ISO), function(v)
  round(cor(gd[[v]], gd$MesoEcoProportionCAC, method = "spearman"), 3))
```

## Groups or gradient? Model comparison

Lower AICc = better support (ΔAICc > 2 is a meaningful difference).

```{r gradient-vs-groups}
aicc <- function(f) { k <- attr(logLik(f), "df"); m <- nobs(f); AIC(f) + 2 * k * (k + 1) / (m - k - 1) }
forms <- list(`Year only`              = "ProcedureYear",
              `Two modes (groups)`     = c("strategy", "ProcedureYear"),
              `Main axis (Dim 1)`      = c("Dim1", "ProcedureYear"),
              `All retained axes`      = c(DIMS, "ProcedureYear"),
              `California Current use` = c("logCAC", "ProcedureYear"))
cmp <- bind_rows(lapply(ISO, function(v) bind_rows(lapply(names(forms), function(nm) {
  f <- lm(reformulate(forms[[nm]], v), data = gd)
  data.frame(isotope = v, model = nm, n_par = attr(logLik(f), "df"), AICc = aicc(f),
             adj_R2 = summary(f)$adj.r.squared)
})) %>% mutate(delta_AICc = AICc - min(AICc)) %>% arrange(delta_AICc)))
cmp %>% mutate(across(where(is.double), ~ round(.x, 3)))
write.csv(cmp, file.path(OUT, "C_groups_vs_gradient_AICc.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r gradient-plot, fig.height = 6}
gp <- gd %>% dplyr::select(strategy, all_of(ISO), Dim1, logCAC) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(ISO), names_to = "isotope", values_to = "value") %>%
  pivot_longer(c(Dim1, logCAC), names_to = "gradient", values_to = "x")
g <- ggplot(gp, aes(x, value)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = strategy), alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, colour = "black") +
  facet_grid(isotope ~ gradient, scales = "free",
             labeller = labeller(gradient = c(Dim1 = "Dim 1 score",
                                              logCAC = "log(California Current proportion)"))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = COLS) + theme_bw() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "‰", colour = "Mode")
g
ggsave(file.path(FIG, "C_isotopes_vs_gradient.pdf"), g, width = 8, height = 6, device = cairo_pdf)
```

**Interpretation.** Evidence for a continuum: (i) weak cluster structure
(null-model p close to 0.05), (ii) a unimodal or only weakly bimodal main axis,
and (iii) isotopes explained by position along the gradient (or by California
Current use) at least as well as by group membership. If so, describe
post-moult foraging as continuous variation along the offshore–latitudinal
gradient, with the two modes as convenient summaries rather than strategies.

# Summary

```{r summary}
list(
  dimensions = c(N_DIM = N_DIM, pct_variance = round(pc_tab$cum_pct[N_DIM], 1)),
  strategies = table(dat$strategy),
  stability_jaccard = round(setNames(jac_cl[size_order], lev), 2),
  sensitivity_ARI = sens_tab,
  isotope_tests = iso_tests %>% dplyr::select(response, covariates, p_perm, p_BH),
  isotope_equivalence = tost %>% dplyr::select(isotope, contrast, estimate, equivalent, different),
  niche_size = size_tab %>% dplyr::select(strategy, n, SEAc, SEAb_median),
  overlap_95 = round(ov_mean[, , 1], 1),
  SIBER_size = if (exists("siber_size")) siber_size else "SIBER not run",
  SIBER_overlap = if (exists("siber_ov")) siber_ov else "SIBER not run",
  null_structure = null_struct,
  isotopes_vs_gradient = grad_tests %>% dplyr::select(response, term, p_perm, p_BH),
  groups_vs_gradient = cmp %>% dplyr::select(isotope, model, delta_AICc, adj_R2))
saveRDS(dat, file.path(OUT, "PM_strategies.rds"))
sessionInfo()
```

# Suggested Methods text (update numbers from the output)

*Foraging strategies of post-moult females were identified with the same
procedure as for the post-breeding trip, from 19 movement, habitat-use and
diving variables summarising each trip (one trip with an impossible value of
the proportion of time diving was excluded). Variables were standardised and
summarised by principal component analysis; the number of components was
chosen by Horn's parallel analysis (1,000 permutations, 95th percentile).
Individuals were clustered on the retained components by Ward's hierarchical
clustering followed by k-means consolidation (HCPC; FactoMineR). Candidate
solutions (k = 2–8) were evaluated with the gap statistic (Tibshirani et al.
2001; 1-SE rule), mean silhouette width, minimum cluster size (≥ 5) and
stability under a whole-pipeline bootstrap (500 resamples; mean Jaccard ≥ 0.75,
Hennig 2007), and the strength of cluster structure was tested against data
simulated from a single multivariate normal distribution. [Report K, the
silhouette null-model p-value, and why K + 1 was rejected.] Because cluster
structure was weak, isotope values were also related to each individual's
position along the behavioural gradient (scores on the retained components),
using Freedman–Lane permutation tests adjusting for the other components and
year, and models based on groups and on the continuous gradient were compared
with AICc. Robustness was assessed by
comparing partitions (adjusted Rand index) obtained with ±1 component,
multiple factor analysis weighting spatial and diving variables equally,
log-transformation of skewed variables, removal of redundant variables and of
multivariate outliers, alternative clustering algorithms, and one trip per
individual. Stable isotope values (δ¹³C, δ¹⁵N) were not used to define
strategies and were analysed independently: differences among strategies were
tested with Freedman–Lane permutation tests including year as a covariate,
equivalence was assessed with two one-sided tests. Isotopic niche width was
estimated as the sample-size-corrected standard ellipse area (SEAc) and its
Bayesian estimate (SEA_B; SIBER, Jackson et al. 2011; 2 chains of 20,000
iterations, burn-in 1,000, thinning 10, default priors). Niche overlap was
estimated as the directional probability that an individual of one strategy
falls within the 95 % niche region of another (nicheROVER, default
non-informative prior; Swanson et al. 2015), and, as a check, as the area
shared by the Bayesian 95 % ellipses relative to their combined area (SIBER).*
